newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Keppel unveils cure for ailing Manila bank.
newsitem.headline: Keppel unveils cure for ailing Manila bank.

text.p: Keppel Corp Ltd said on Monday it will automate operations of Philippines' Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank which it rescued from cash flow problems early this month.
The Singapore-based firm said in a statement the automation of the 31 branches of Monte de Piedad was part of new measures to strengthen the bank.

"In addition to the use of information technology, the Keppel management will send bank officers to the group's operations in Singapore for training," it said in a statement issued by its local subsidiary Keppel Philippines Holdings Inc.
Keppel also plans to open six more Monte de Piedad branches nationwide within the year, and to convert it into a commercial bank.

"Monte de Piedad will soon launch a series of new products for customers followings (its) reorganisation," Keppel said. "While the bank intends to retain its current depositors, we would also want to extend our businesses to corporate enterprises."
"There are many businesses that we can do...these include trust funds, real estate, club membership, motor vehicles, and equipment loans," Keppel said.
Monte de Piedad also hopes to be active in the treasury business, said president Fidel Bugayong, a former executive director of Keppel's investment house in the Philippines.
Keppel said it had implemented internal control measures on the bank which faced financial problems after a lending programme to small entrepreneurs failed.
"These include approval limits for loans and interest rate fixing. The bank has also introduced credit policies with proper screening criteria," it added.
